'''David Essex''' (born '''David Albert Cook'''; 23 July 1947)<ref name="British Hit Singles & Albums">{{cite book |first=David |last=Roberts |year=2006 |title=British Hit Singles & Albums |edition=19 |publisher=Guinness World Records |location=London |isbn=1-904994-10-5 |pages=186–187}}</ref> is an English singer-songwriter and actor. From 1973 to 1994, he had nineteen Top-40 singles in the UK (including two number ones) and sixteen Top-40 albums.<ref name="British Hit Singles & Albums"/> Internationally, he had the most success with his 1973 single "[[Rock On (David Essex song)|Rock On]]".

Essex has also had an extensive career as an actor, which includes a nomination for the [[BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles]] for the film [[That'll Be the Day (film)|''That'll Be the Day'']] (1973) and a nomination for the [[Laurence Olivier Award for Best Performance in a Musical]] for [[Evita (musical)|''Evita'']] in [[1978 Laurence Olivier Awards|1978]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most Promising Newcomer To Leading Film Roles |url=https://www.bafta.org/awards/film/most-promising-newcomer-to-leading-film-roles |access-date=2025-02-12 |website=Bafta |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Olivier Winners 1978 |url=https://officiallondontheatre.com/olivier-awards/winners/olivier-winners-1978/ |access-date=2025-02-12 |website=Olivier Awards |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Early life==
Essex was born in [[Plaistow, Newham|Plaistow]], [[Essex]] (now an area in the [[London Borough of Newham]], included within [[Greater London]]) on 23 July 1947.<ref name="Fielding 18">Sarah Fielding. "From Rags to 'Rock On': How David Essex Became a Star." ''Music Scene.'' [https://archive.org/details/MusicSceneDecember197312/page/n15/mode/2up December 1973.] p. 18.</ref> His father, Albert, was an East End docker and his mother, Olive (née Kemp), was a self-taught pianist and an [[Irish Traveller]]. His grandfather, Thomas Kemp, was nicknamed "Philimore", which was the anglicised version of "Philly Mor" – being Irish for "Big Philly". Essex was two years old when his parents moved out of the overcrowded home the family was sharing with relatives, to [[Canning Town]] where he grew up.

Essex attended Star Lane Primary School. He loved playing football and did not answer any of the questions in the [[Eleven plus exam]] for entry into a [[grammar school]], so that he could ensure he attended Shipman County Secondary School where he knew they played the game. He later attended The Warren secondary modern in Whalebone Lane, [[Chadwell Heath]], when his parents moved to Marks Gate Estate.<ref name=CharmedLife>{{cite book |title=A Charmed Life: The Autobiography of David Essex: Amazon.co.uk: David Essex: 9780752851600: Books |id={{ASIN|0752851608|country=uk}} }}</ref> He was also a member of [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] Juniors for a while, and dreamed of one day being a professional player.<ref>[http://www.thebiographychannel.co.uk/biography_story/1797:2247/1/David_Essex.htm "David Essex" biography] at Biography Channel: Music Stars. ({{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070118155247/http://www.thebiographychannel.co.uk/biography_story/1797%3A2247/1/David_Essex.htm |date=18 January 2007}})</ref>  He then also became interested in music and played drums with a local band (China Plates), before becoming a singer.<ref name="Fielding 18"/>

==Career==
===Early career===
Essex made his first record, titled "And the Tears Came Tumbling Down",<ref name="Murrells1978"/> for the [[Fontana Records|Fontana]] label<ref>David Essex, "Over The Moon" page 70 ("with my new name on the label next to the famous blue and white Fontana logo"), Virgin Books 2012, {{ISBN|978-0-7535-4033-6}}</ref> in 1965. He then toured with a band called 'David Essex and the Mood Indigo' for two years, and released a further seven singles in the 1960s. He also recorded two songs, "A Rose" and "Leon and John and Billy and Me" which remain unreleased, but exist as acetates. His first notable acting role, aside from small appearances in the films ''[[Assault (film)|Assault]]'' and ''[[All Coppers Are...]]'',<ref name="Murrells1978"/> was the lead in the [[Musical theatre|stage musical]] ''[[Godspell]]''<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/programmes/breakfast/2220580.stm |title=Rags to riches tale of Essex boy David |work=[[BBC News]] |date=28 August 2002 |access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref><ref name="Fielding 17">Sarah Fielding. "From Rags to 'Rock On': How David Essex Became a Star." ''Music Scene.'' [https://archive.org/details/MusicSceneDecember197312/page/n15/mode/2up December 1973.] p. 17.</ref> in 1971 at the age of 23.

Two years later, he starred in the film ''[[That'll Be the Day (film)|That'll Be the Day]]'' (1973)<ref name="NME Rock 'N' Roll Years">{{cite book |first=John |last=Tobler |year=1992 |title=NME Rock 'N' Roll Years |edition=1st |publisher=Reed International Books Ltd |location=London |page=243 |id=CN 5585}}</ref> and recorded his international hit single, the self-penned "[[Rock On (David Essex song)|Rock On]]", in the same year.<ref name="Murrells1978"/> It sold over one million copies, and was awarded a [[music recording sales certification|gold disc]] by the [[R.I.A.A.]] in March 1974.<ref name="Murrells1978">{{cite book|author=Joseph Murrells|title=The Book of Golden Discs|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UxRAAAAAMAAJ&q=Dodie+Stevens+%22Pink+ShoeLaces%22|year=1978|publisher=Barrie and Jenkins|isbn=978-0-214-20480-7|page=327}}</ref> It was nominated for a Grammy and reached No. 5 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref name="Murrells1978"/> A second single, "Lamplight", also reached the Top 10 in the [[UK singles chart]].

In the 1970s, Essex emerged as a performer of some note. Contrary to a claim made in his own biography, his first concert was at the Granada in [[East Ham]] on Saturday 2 November 1974, and not at the Odeon. His biggest hits during this decade included two UK [[Chart-topper|number one]] singles: "[[Gonna Make You a Star]]" (1974) and "[[Hold Me Close]]" (1975). He also appeared in ''[[Stardust (1974 film)|Stardust]]'', a 1974 sequel to ''[[That'll Be the Day (film)|That'll Be the Day]]''.<ref name="five">{{cite magazine|magazine=Filmink|first=Stephen|last=Vagg|url=https://www.filmink.com.au/forgotten-british-film-moguls-nat-cohen-part-five-1971-1988/|access-date=5 February 2025|date=5 February 2025|title=Forgotten British film moguls – Nat Cohen: Part Five (1971-1988)}}</ref><ref name="NME Rock 'N' Roll Years 2">{{cite book |first=John |last=Tobler |year=1992 |title=NME Rock 'N' Roll Years |publisher=Reed International Books Ltd |location=London |edition=1st |page=254 |id=CN 5585}}</ref> The title song was another Top 10 hit. In 1976, Essex covered [[the Beatles]] song "[[Yesterday (song)|Yesterday]]" for the musical documentary ''[[All This and World War II]]''.

Essex's pop idol looks gave him a strong female fan base, and his British tours created scenes of hysteria reminiscent of [[Beatlemania]]. According to ''The Guinness Book of British Hit Singles'',<ref>{{cite book |first=David |last=Roberts |year=2006 |title=British Hit Singles & Albums |edition=16 |publisher=Guinness World Records |location=London |isbn=0-85112-190-X|pages=181–182}}</ref> he was voted the number one British male vocalist in 1974, and was a teen idol for more than a decade.

===Musical roles===
After a couple of years (from November 1971) playing the lead in ''Godspell'' in London, in December 1973 Essex appeared in the stage version of ''Tommy'' at London's Rainbow Theatre.<ref name="NME Rock 'N' Roll Years 3">{{cite book |first=John |last=Tobler |year=1992 |title=NME Rock 'N' Roll Years |publisher=Reed International Books Ltd |location=London |edition=1st |page=257 |id=CN 5585}}</ref>

In 1978, he appeared on [[Jeff Wayne]]'s [[Jeff Wayne's Musical Version of The War of the Worlds|musical version of ''The War of the Worlds'']], as the Artilleryman. In the UK the two-record set remains a best-seller.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.war-ofthe-worlds.co.uk/music_mars.htm |title=History of Jeff Wayne's musical version of The War of the Worlds, part 1. War of the Worlds Invasion website |work=War-ofthe-worlds.co.uk |date=28 May 1953 |access-date=26 August 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120329142255/http://www.war-ofthe-worlds.co.uk/music_mars.htm |archive-date=29 March 2012 }}</ref>

In the same year, Essex played the character [[Che Guevara|Che]] in the original production of [[Tim Rice]] and [[Andrew Lloyd Webber]]'s musical ''[[Evita (musical)|Evita]]'',<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Rich |first=Frank |url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,919829,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071224122540/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,919829,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 December 2007 |title=Theater: Eva Peron, Superstar |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=21 August 1978 |access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref> and his recording of the show's "[[Oh What a Circus]]"<ref>[http://www.andrewlloydwebber.com/sections/recordings/music_topten.php] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070501175349/http://www.andrewlloydwebber.com/sections/recordings/music_topten.php|date=1 May 2007}}</ref> reached number three. As the best known of the principal performers, Essex actually received top billing, above [[Elaine Paige]] whose stardom seemingly arrived overnight with her casting in the show.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Rice|first=Tim|title=Oh, What a Circus: The Autobiography|publisher=Hodder & Stoughton|year=1999|isbn=0340648953|location=London|pages=406, 410}}</ref> His contract required him to remain with the show for just five and a half months, during which, unusually and as Essex had predicted, his understudy, [[Nigel Planer]], was never required to perform.

Two years later, he starred in the motorcycle racing film ''[[Silver Dream Racer]]'';<ref name="timing">{{cite magazine|first=Stephen|last=Vagg|magazine=Filmink|date=1 September 2025|access-date=1 September 2025|url=https://www.filmink.com.au/forgotten-british-film-studios-the-rank-organisation-1978-81/|title=Forgotten British Film Studios: The Rank Organisation 1978-81}}</ref> and the [[soundtrack]] song "[[Silver Dream Machine]]" was a top five hit in the UK singles chart. Essex, a keen motorcyclist, waived his fee for the then-new 1980 electric-start [[Triumph Bonneville T140|Triumph Bonneville]] he had contracted to advertise on behalf of the struggling [[Triumph Engineering Company|Triumph motorcycle workers' co-operative]].<ref>Rosamond, John, ''Save The Triumph Bonneville! The Inside Story Of The Meriden Workers' Co-Op'' {{ISBN|1845842650}}</ref>

In 1981, he starred in ''[[Childe Byron]]'', a play staged at the [[Young Vic]] theatre.

In 1985, he co-wrote and starred as [[Fletcher Christian]] in the [[West End theatre|West End]] musical [[Mutiny (musical)|''Mutiny!'']], based on the novel ''[[Mutiny on the Bounty (novel)|Mutiny on the Bounty]]'' by Charles Nordhoff and James Norman Hall. The score produced two more hit singles, including "Tahiti", his tenth Top 10 success.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.indielondon.co.uk/Theatre-Review/david-essex-and-a-new-musical |title=All the Fun of the Fair – New Wimbledon Theatre – Your London Reviews |publisher=IndieLondon |access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref>

In February 2016, Essex performed in the West End production of ''Jeff Wayne's Musical Version of The War Of The Worlds'' at London's [[Dominion Theatre]] as the Voice of Humanity.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.londontheatredirect.com/news/1733/Casting-Announced-For-Jeff-Wayne-s-Musical-Phenomenon-The-War-Of-The-Worlds-With-Liam-Neeson-In-3D-Hologram.aspx |title=Casting Announced For Jeff Wayne's Musical Phenomenon The War Of The Worlds With Liam Neeson In 3D Hologram |work=London Theatre Direct |access-date=24 January 2016 |date=21 January 2016 |author=Porteous, Jacob|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20250502110956/https://www.londontheatredirect.com/news/casting-announced-for-jeff-waynes-musical-phenomenon-the-war-of-the-worlds-with-liam-neeson-in-3d-hologram|archive-date=2 May 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Later career===
Essex continued to perform in all areas of [[show business]]. A 1988 sitcom, ''[[The River (UK TV series)|The River]]'', achieved good ratings. In 1991, a music compilation entitled ''His Greatest Hits'' reached number 13; a 1993 album, ''Cover Shot'', featuring a cover version of the [[Buzz Cason]]/[[Mac Gayden]] song "[[Everlasting Love]]", peaked at number 3. His autobiography, ''A Charmed Life'', was published in 2002, and became a best-seller.

In the [[1999 New Year Honours]], Essex was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) "for charitable services, especially to Voluntary Service Overseas."<ref>UK list: {{London Gazette |date=31 December 1998 |supp=1 |issue=55354 |pages=10}}</ref> He still tours the UK every year and releases albums through his website. Despite his long and successful British career, he remains largely unknown in the United States. "[[Rock On (David Essex song)|Rock On]]" reached number three in 1974 and was his only US ''[[Cash Box]]'' Top 40 [[hit single]].

Essex, who comes from a family of [[Irish Travellers]], played a kind-hearted nomad in one episode of [[ITV1]]'s 1960s [[Yorkshire]]-based drama ''[[Heartbeat (British TV series)|Heartbeat]]'' in 2000. He played a character called Johnny Lee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0599022/ |title="Heartbeat" – The Traveller |date=2000 |work=IMDb |access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref> Essex told Jake Bowers of the BBC's ''[[Rokker Radio]]'', a programme for Gypsies and Travellers, on 30 July 2006, that he has always been openly proud of his Traveller family history. He was Patron of Britain's National Gypsy Council, which works for equal rights, education, and services for [[Romani people|Romany]] and [[Irish Travellers]].<ref name="autogenerated1" />

In 2005, he appeared as a guest vocalist on, and wrote songs for, [[Saint Etienne (band)|Saint Etienne]]'s album ''[[Tales from Turnpike House]]''.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/6music/whatson/aotd/aotd_etienne_turnpike.shtml] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081118055925/http://www.bbc.co.uk/6music/whatson/aotd/aotd_etienne_turnpike.shtml|date=18 November 2008}}</ref> Also that year, he appeared in the [[Channel 4]] [[Documentary film|documentary]] ''[[Bring Back...The Christmas Number One]]''.

Essex was due to join the cast of [[soap opera]] ''[[EastEnders]]'', in early 2006, as new character [[Jack Edwards (EastEnders)|Jack Edwards]], but the role was expanded beyond the three weeks planned, and Essex was unable to commit the time.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/4491932.stm |title=Essex withdraws from EastEnders |work=BBC News |date=2 December 2005 |access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref> The role instead went to [[Nicky Henson]].

A model and recording of Essex is featured in the museum of [[West Ham United Football Club]]. In the recording, he explains his reasons for supporting West Ham and his love of the team.

Essex spent six years as an ambassador for [[Voluntary Service Overseas]], which earned him an OBE in 1999.<ref name="autogenerated1"/>

===Recent years===
Essex used to record and release records on his own [[record label]], Lamplight. He has since changed the name of his company to Joseph Webster Ltd, named after his first grandchild. He tours regularly and continues to act, appearing in ''Boogie Nights 2'', ''[[Footloose (2011 film)|Footloose]]'' and [[Andrew Lloyd Webber]]'s musical ''[[Aspects of Love]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thisistheatre.com/regional/aspects-of-love.html |title=Aspects of Love musical on stage: Ticket and UK tour information |publisher=Thisistheatre.com |access-date=26 August 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151017060233/http://www.thisistheatre.com/regional/aspects-of-love.html |archive-date=17 October 2015 }}</ref> From September 2008 to the summer of 2009 he took his own musical, ''All the Fun of the Fair'', on a tour of the United Kingdom. He followed this in the autumn with a sell-out solo tour of the UK, named the Secret Tour. Essex has released a [[DVD]] on his website of the last night of the tour, filmed in [[Bournemouth]]. He returned to London's West End with ''All the Fun of the Fair'' but with a different ending from that performed in the provinces.

In January 2011, it was announced that Essex had finally joined the cast of ''[[EastEnders]]'' as [[Eddie Moon]], five years after he was initially supposed to appear in the show.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/soaps/s2/eastenders/news/a299682/david-essex-lands-eastenders-role.html |title=David Essex lands 'EastEnders' role |last=Kilkelly |first=Daniel |date=24 January 2011 |work=[[Digital Spy]] |publisher=[[Hachette Filipacchi Médias|Hachette Filipacchi (UK) Ltd]] |access-date=24 January 2011}}</ref> His first on-screen appearance was on 3 June 2011. Eddie left the square on 6 October 2011. He then wrote the music score for the film ''Traveller'' (2013), in which he co-starred with his son who played the main role as a half-gypsy trying to find his identity.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.romfordrecorder.co.uk/news/21545722.david-essex-launches-new-film-romford/|title=David Essex launches new film in Romfo|first=Sam|last=Gelder|date=10 December 2013|accessdate=15 January 2024|work=[[Romford Recorder]]|publisher=[[Newsquest Media Group]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On 20 September 2010, Essex married Welsh actress Susan Hallam-Wright (born 1973) his third wife, at St Cross Church, Talybont, near [[Bangor, Gwynedd|Bangor]], [[North Wales]]. He first met her at the end of 2008 when she was auditioning for a role in ''All the Fun of the Fair''. Essex had previously been married to Maureen Neal (in 1971) and Carlotta Christy (in 1997).<ref>David Essex, ''Over the Moon'', Virgin Books, 2012, {{ISBN|978-0-7535-4033-6}}</ref>

Essex has five children: two with his first wife, twins with his second wife and a fourth son with his third wife.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.smoothradio.com/news/music/david-essex-age-wife-children-songs/|title=David Essex facts: Singer's age, wife, children, songs and career revealed|accessdate=15 January 2024|work=[[Smooth Radio (2014)|Smooth Radio]]|date=2 July 2022}}</ref>
